question.text: A diatomic molecule has a dipole moment of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.2</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></math>. If the bond distance is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mover></math>, then fractional charge on each atom is _____  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> esu. (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>esu</mi><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>)

solution.text:
Given,

 μ=1.2Dμ=q×dwhere, μ = dipole moment  q = charge d= distance

q= 1.2 D1.0A0  

∴q=1.2×10−10 esu

Hence, the charge present on each atom is approximately zero.
